content: 1. Ethinylestradiol and Mineral Oil: Mineral oil can reduce the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 2. Ethinylestradiol and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 3. Ethinylestradiol and Tricyclic Antidepressants (TCAs): Ethinylestradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of TCAs, potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of adverse effects. This interaction applies to medications such as nortriptyline, protriptyline, amitriptyline, and others. 4. Ethinylestradiol and Ramelteon: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 5. Ribociclib and Norethindrone: Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 6. Rosuvastatin and Ethinylestradiol: Rosuvastatin increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 7. Acitretin and Norethindrone: Acitretin reduces the effects of norethindrone through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. This combination is contraindicated, and alternative contraceptive methods should be used. 8. Ethinylestradiol and Albiglutide: Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Oral Contraceptives and Antidiabetics: Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 10. Ethinylestradiol and Alprazolam: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This may lead to higher serum concentrations of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation. Close monitoring is recommended. 11. Ethinylestradiol and Aminocaproic Acid: Concomitant use may result in additive hypercoagulability due to increased clotting factor production and inhibition of fibrinolysis. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Ethinylestradiol and Amobarbital: Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Ethinylestradiol and Amoxicillin: Amoxicillin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Ethinylestradiol and Anastrozole: Anastrozole decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens should not be used concurrently with anastrozole. 15. Ethinylestradiol and Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 16. Ethinylestradiol and Armodafinil: Armodafinil reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 17. Ethinylestradiol and Antibiotics (e.g., Cefaclor, Cefadroxil, Cefdinir): Antibiotics may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Ethinylestradiol and Brigatinib: Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 19. Ethinylestradiol and Cimetidine: Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Ethinylestradiol and Clindamycin: Clindamycin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Ethinylestradiol and Clobazam: Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 22. Ethinylestradiol and Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Ethinylestradiol and Dexamethasone: Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 24. Ethinylestradiol and Diazepam: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of diazepam by decreasing its metabolism. This may lead to higher serum concentrations of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation. Close monitoring is recommended. 25. Ethinylestradiol and Doxycycline: Doxycycline may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Ethinylestradiol and Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 27. Ethinylestradiol and Elagolix: Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 28. Ethinylestradiol and Elvitegravir: Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 29. Ethinylestradiol and Danazol: Danazol increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Ethinylestradiol and Darunavir: Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when ethinylestradiol is coadministered with other medications, as these interactions can impact drug efficacy and safety.
